issues.display_title: Issue #126: Implement POST /v1/support/feedback/:id/reply with email delivery
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 11/08/26

✅ Implementation: Support Feedback Reply ( Task #126 / PR #138 )

Summary

Implemented issue #126: authenticated support users can reply to feedback by email through Plunk. A reply is added to history only after email delivery succeeds, then the feedback status changes to replied.

Endpoint

POST /v1/support/feedback/:id/reply
Authorization: Bearer <support-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "message": "Thanks for your feedback. We fixed the issue."
}

The route uses the existing middleware.Auth() and middleware.SupportOnly() guards.

Behavior

  • Trims message and rejects missing, empty, or whitespace-only values with 400.
  • Returns 404 when the feedback ID is unknown.
  • Sends email synchronously to the email snapshot stored on the feedback record. No live user lookup is performed.
  • Returns 502 when Plunk delivery fails and leaves reply history and feedback status unchanged.
  • After successful delivery, creates the reply and changes feedback status to replied in one database transaction.
  • Stores sender user ID, name and email snapshots, recipient email snapshot, message, and creation time.
  • Returns 201 with the created reply.
  • If persistence fails after delivery, returns 500 with reply email was sent but saving it failed - do not retry. This warns the support agent against sending a duplicate email.

Plunk Template

Template ID:

6addbbd0-f108-4b6f-af50-90823b0ffe39

Template data:

  • fullname: feedback submitter name snapshot
  • email: feedback submitter email snapshot
  • message: trimmed support reply

EmailService.SendFeedbackReplyEmail follows the existing trigger() pattern and uses the existing USEPLUNK_URL and USEPLUNK_SECRET_KEY settings.

Files Changed

  • src/config/templates.go
  • src/services/email.go
  • src/services/email_test.go
  • src/action/v1/feedback/reply.go
  • src/action/v1/feedback/reply_test.go
  • src/controllers/v1/feedback/create.go
  • src/routes/v1/feedback.go
  • src/routes/v1/support_feedback_test.go
  • api-collection/v1/feedback/Reply to support feedback.yml

No model or migration changes were needed because FeedbackReply already existed.

Tests

Coverage includes:

  • Correct Plunk template, recipient, and data.
  • Successful email delivery, reply history creation, sender/recipient snapshots, timestamp, and replied status.
  • Empty message returns 400.
  • Unknown feedback returns 404.
  • Unauthenticated and non-support requests return 401 and 403.
  • Plunk failure returns 502, creates no reply, and preserves the previous status.
  • Database failure after delivery returns an explicit do not retry warning.

Verification commands:

go test -count=1 ./src/action/v1/feedback/... ./src/routes/v1/... ./src/services/...
go build ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

All checks passed. A real Plunk message using this template was also delivered successfully to the requested test inbox.

Known Limitation

Email and database writes are two separate systems. If email succeeds but persistence fails, the email cannot be recalled. Full idempotency would require an outbox or idempotency key and a schema change; it is outside issue #126.

PRD #120 section 7. FE counterpart: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#578.

Description

Support replies to a feedback submitter by email, and the reply is recorded in history.

External blocker — Plunk template

All transactional email goes through Plunk (src/services/email.go), with template IDs as compile-time constants in src/config/templates.go. A new "support reply" template must be created in the Plunk dashboard before this can be finished — the reply body is free-form text, so the template needs a long-text variable for the message. Get the template ID first; the code change is small once it exists.

Acceptance Criteria

  • POST /v1/support/feedback/:id/reply behind middleware.Auth() + SupportOnly()
  • Non-empty message required → 400 when empty
  • New TemplateSupportReply constant in src/config/templates.go
  • New SendFeedbackReplyEmail method on EmailService, following the existing trigger() pattern
  • Email is sent to the feedback's stored user email snapshot, not to a live user lookup
  • Email send happens before the reply row is written. A failed send must leave no reply history record.
  • Reply stores sender name and email snapshots, recipient email, message, created_at
  • Feedback status moves to replied after a successful reply
  • Errors: 401, 403 non-support, 400 empty message, 404 unknown ID, 502 on email delivery failure
  • Tests: successful reply sends to the submitter's stored email; reply history created with sender name/email/message/timestamp; status becomes replied; empty message → 400; unknown ID → 404; non-support → 403; simulated email failure → 502 and no reply row created
  • api-collection/v1 entry added
  • Manual end-to-end check: real reply email received

Dependencies

#121 (SupportOnly guard), #122 (models), Plunk template ID.

RESULT 11/08/26

✅ Implementation: Support Feedback Pagination ( Task #136 / PR #139 )

Summary

Implemented issue #136 in PR #139: GET /v1/support/feedback now returns a bounded page instead of every matching feedback row. The existing data.feedback array remains unchanged, with pagination metadata added beside it.

API

GET /v1/support/feedback?page=1&per_page=20
Authorization: Bearer <support-token>

Pagination composes with all existing list parameters:

  • search
  • status
  • category
  • area
  • project_id
  • sort
  • page
  • per_page

Defaults and Validation

  • Default page: 1
  • Default per_page: 20
  • Maximum per_page: 100
  • Either parameter may be omitted independently.
  • Non-numeric, zero, negative, or over-limit values return 400.
  • Page values that would overflow the SQL offset calculation also return 400.
  • A page after the final result returns 200 with an empty feedback array.

Response

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "requestTime": 1,
  "data": {
    "feedback": [],
    "total": 0,
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 20
  }
}

total counts every row matching the active filters before LIMIT and OFFSET are applied.

Query Behavior

The same filtered GORM query is used for the total count and paginated rows. Existing deterministic ordering remains intact because every sort mode retains id ASC as its final tie-breaker. This prevents duplicates or missing rows while traversing a fixed dataset page by page.

Reply history is no longer preloaded by the list endpoint. Full ordered history remains available from GET /v1/support/feedback/:id. This reduces list query work and response size.

Files Changed

  • src/action/v1/feedback/read.go
  • src/action/v1/feedback/read_test.go
  • api-collection/v1/feedback/List support feedback.yml

No schema, migration, route, or model changes were required.

Tests

Coverage includes:

  • Default pagination metadata.
  • Explicit page and per_page.
  • Independent defaults when either parameter is omitted.
  • Short final page.
  • Page beyond the result set.
  • Invalid numeric values, values above the cap, and offset overflow.
  • Totals under search, status, category, area, and project_id filters.
  • Pagination with newest, oldest, recently_updated, and status sorting.
  • No duplicate or missing rows when walking every page.

Verification commands:

go test ./src/action/v1/feedback -count=1
go build ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

The feature-specific tests, build, vet, and diff check passed during implementation. The repository-wide suite had one unrelated pre-existing failure in TestPredictStreamsSSEEvents: the test expects /predict/txt, while the current implementation calls /txt.

PRD #120 section 4. FE counterpart: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#578. Follow-up to #124 (PR #135).

Description

GET /v1/support/feedback currently returns every matching row in one response, and preloads the full reply history for each one. There is no limit, offset, or total count.

Raised during review of PR #135 and deliberately left out of #124, whose acceptance criteria do not mention pagination.

Why

The support inbox only grows. Every list call fetches all feedback plus all replies, and search runs LOWER(...) LIKE '%term%' across six columns, which cannot use an index. The response also has no total, so the frontend cannot show a count or build a pager without receiving the entire table first.

This is safe to add later because the current response is {"data": {"feedback": [...]}} — adding sibling keys alongside feedback is additive and does not break GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#578.

Acceptance Criteria

  • page and per_page query parameters on GET /v1/support/feedback
  • Sensible defaults when either is omitted, and a hard upper bound on per_page
  • Invalid values (non-numeric, zero, negative, above the cap) → 400, consistent with how status and sort are already validated
  • Response keeps the existing feedback array and adds total count plus current page/per-page alongside it — existing consumers of data.feedback keep working unchanged
  • Pagination composes with every existing filter (search, status, category, area, project_id) and with all four sort modes
  • Ordering stays deterministic across pages — the existing id ASC tie-breaker must survive, so no row is repeated or skipped between page boundaries
  • Count query respects the same filters as the page query
  • Decide whether replies should still be preloaded for the list, or fetched only in the detail endpoint
  • Tests: default paging; explicit page/per_page; last page shorter than per_page; page past the end returns empty rather than an error; per_page above the cap → 400; invalid values → 400; totals correct under a filter; no duplicate or missing rows when walking every page of a fixed dataset
  • api-collection/v1/feedback/List support feedback.yml updated with the new parameters

Dependencies

#124 (list endpoint) — merged as PR #135.
